comparison: Both evaluate p38 MAPK as downstream mediator of FYN-driven resistance (C41, C43, C44, C90). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of context-dependency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'the study does not fully explore...the downstream pathways through which FYN upregulation confers drug resistance,' indicating incomplete mechanistic understanding.

Both evaluate in vivo validation (C72, C74). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this is SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly praise 'potent in vivo efficacy of certain combination treatments, underscoring the clinical relevance' with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate FYN as general mediator of drug tolerance across cancer types (C7, C8, C76, C78, C79, C82, C83, C87). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED but note 'FYN has been implicated in drug resistance in previous studies...it does not present entirely novel findings regarding FYN's role,' tempering enthusiasm about novelty while acknowledging value.

Both evaluate library construction and screening methodology (C20-C27, C30-C31). OpenEval finds comprehensive validation SUPPORTED with high coverage and strong correlations. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, praising 'large combination matrix of druggable tyrosine kinase gene knockouts' that 'mitigates off-target effects' with no concerns about methodology.

Both evaluate KDM4-mediated epigenetic regulation of FYN (C5, C64, C66-C69, C106). OpenEval finds strong mechanistic evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating evidence is 'solid' but 'the study does not fully explore the upstream mechanisms regulating KDM4A,' indicating incomplete understanding limits claim strength.

Both evaluate FYN validation as synergistic target with TKIs (C36-C38). OpenEval finds comprehensive validation SUPPORTED across multiple methods. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'successfully reveals FYN as a mediator' but noting 'combination of FYN knockout with other gene knockouts exhibits only very modest synergy' with 'high standard deviation,' weakening genetic validation despite stronger pharmacological effects.

Both evaluate TKI-induced FYN upregulation via KDM4 mechanism (C4, C45, C52, C54, C58). OpenEval finds mechanistic link SUPPORTED with temporal relationships and systematic testing. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, describing evidence as 'solid' but noting incomplete exploration of 'upstream mechanisms regulating KDM4A,' limiting mechanistic completeness.

Both evaluate summary conclusions about FYN and combination therapy (C3, C6, C85). OpenEval finds conclusions SUPPORTED by collective evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the study 'successfully reveals FYN as a mediator' but noting modest genetic synergy and high variability weaken robustness of overall conclusions.

Both evaluate FYN as priority target including TNBC-specific upregulation (C35) and clinical correlations (C59-C60, C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through network centrality and differential expression. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, describing findings as 'valuable' with 'solid' evidence and acknowledging clinical relevance for 'potential targets for combination therapy.'

Both evaluate clinical relevance via survival analysis (C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED while appropriately noting correlation doesn't establish causality. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, describing findings as 'valuable' with no specific concerns about correlative analyses.

Both evaluate validation of screen hits (C30-C31). OpenEval finds 75% validation rate and strong correlation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find screening approach SUPPORTED, praising the methodology with no concerns raised about validation metrics.

Both address context-dependent KDM4 regulation (C84). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as part of broader analysis showing FYN as common node despite mechanistic heterogeneity. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting this aligns with incomplete understanding of 'upstream mechanisms regulating KDM4A' and acknowledging transparent reporting.

Both evaluate validation across multiple cell lines (C39). OpenEval finds reproducibility SUPPORTED as part of comprehensive FYN validation. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting authors 'demonstrate the importance of FYN in drug resistance in multiple ways' though genetic knockout synergy is modest.
